newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hoping to export rich barley crop - ONIC.
newsitem.headline: France hoping to export rich barley crop - ONIC.

text.p: France is hoping to sell a large part of its bumper barley crop on world markets in the new 1996/97 campaign,the head of France's grain office said on Wednesday.
But it will have to compete against some of its EU neighbours also faced with ample supplies.
Speaking at a monthly news conference, ONIC's director general Alain Moulinier said an export target of 1.8 million tonnes was ambitious but would allow France to return to decent export levels.
He said top feed barley importer Saudi Arabia was one of the outlets with which France was hoping to do business this season.
In its first supply/demand report for 1996/97, ONIC predicted French barley exports to non-EU countries might jump to 1.8 million tonnes from just 221,000 tonnes last year.
Barley exports to the rest of the EU, however, might decline to 1.93 million tonnes from 2.24 million as a good crop is forecast throughout the EU.
Moulinier confirmed earlier trade reports that Saudi Arabia had recently bought 800,000 tonnes of feed barley, of which some 600,000 tonnes would come from the European Union.
Most of the EU share of the contract was expected to be covered from German intervention stores.
But France was hoping the European Commission would also allow some barley exports from the free market.
He explained that only free-market exports would allow countries faced with ample suplies at home to avoid selling their grain into intervention stores.

"To avoid possible sales to intervention stores we need to export 1.8 million tonnes outside the European Union. Since the EU has a good crop, we need to export a good quantity from the free market," he said.

Moulinier welcomed signs that the European Commission was relaxing its tight grip on barley exports, having already authorised the export of small tonnages of free-market barley at a refund through its weekly grain tender system.
"One can see the EU is reacting," he said, adding this should open "good opportunities" for France.
ONIC is pegging the French 1996 barley harvest at 9.357 million tonnes against 7.739 million tonnes in 1995.
